title: Mailchimp vs Heap: Product analytics or email marketing and automation?
description: A practical decision guide for teams weighing Mailchimp against Heap. Mailchimp focuses on product analytics, while Heap focuses on email marketing and automation. Use the workflow criteria below to decide whether you need one, the other, or both; verify current vendor capabilities, terms, and pricing before committing.

features.name: Core task
features.tool1Detail: Use Heap to investigate product behavior and user journeys; test event capture, data quality, privacy controls, and whether insights answer product questions.
features.tool2Detail: Use Mailchimp to manage email audiences, campaigns, and automation; test segmentation, deliverability, consent, and reporting.

features.name: Selection test
features.tool1: Run Mailchimp through a representative task and document results, setup effort, and gaps.
features.tool1Detail: Confirm must-have requirements before evaluating plans or switching tools.
features.tool2: Run Heap through the same decision process.
features.tool2Detail: Check whether it solves the same requirement or a separate one.

features.name: Operational checks
features.tool1: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and who will maintain the workflow.
features.tool1Detail: Use vendor documentation and a small pilot; do not infer capabilities from a generic feature checklist.
features.tool2: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and who will maintain the workflow.
features.tool2Detail: Estimate total cost from current plans and actual usage, not an unverified headline price.

features.name: Relationship
features.tool1: Measuring product behavior versus communicating with an audience
features.tool1Detail: Do not treat either product as a universal winner; compare it with the job it is meant to do.
features.tool2: Measuring product behavior versus communicating with an audience
features.tool2Detail: If responsibilities are distinct, using both may make sense; confirm the handoff and avoid paying twice for the same capability.

verdict: There is no evidence-based universal winner between Mailchimp and Heap because their primary jobs differ. Choose Mailchimp if the need described above matches your workflow; choose Heap if its job is the one you need to solve. If both needs exist, assess whether the tools complement each other and define ownership at the handoff. Pilot the relevant workflow, verify current features and plan limits with each vendor, and compare total cost, integrations, privacy, permissions, and support before buying.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Mailchimp and Heap?
faqs.answer: Mailchimp focuses on product analytics, while Heap focuses on email marketing and automation. Start with the job your team needs to complete rather than comparing them as interchangeable products.

faqs.question: Can Mailchimp replace Heap?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. A replacement only makes sense if Mailchimp demonstrably covers the requirements you currently rely on Heap for. Test the real workflow and confirm missing integrations, controls, or outputs before switching.

faqs.question: Can a team use Mailchimp and Heap together?
faqs.answer: Potentially, when the team needs both product analytics and email marketing and automation. Define which tool owns each step, how information moves between them, and who maintains access and data quality.

faqs.question: How should I compare their costs?
faqs.answer: Check each vendor's current pricing and plan limits, then estimate total cost for the seats, usage, integrations, support, and administration required. Do not rely on stale prices or unverified rating claims.

faqs.question: What is the safest way to choose?
faqs.answer: Write down must-have outcomes, run a small pilot using a representative scenario, check security and privacy requirements, and score the results against those outcomes. Verify vendor claims directly.
